info.name: Vigilo Framework API
info.description:
Vigilo Framework REST API.

Base path: `/vf` on port 8086.
Auth: send the JWT user key in the `API_KEY` header. Get one via **Users > Authenticate** (public) — its post-response script stores it into the active environment automatically, so every protected request works afterward. Lambda runtime state, variables, execution, and alerts use `LAMBDA_API_KEY`.

JSON responses share a base envelope: `resultCode`, `resultCodeMessage`, `collectionTotalSize`, `resultCodeDesc`. A successful lambda-variable GET instead returns raw bytes, or HTTP 204 when absent.

exec: console.log('Stored apiKey into the active environment.');

request.description: Authenticates a login account; resident records cannot log in. Returns user and API key, without a resident location.
Administrator only. Registers a developer login account. Use Residents for monitored people with no credentials.

Search non-deleted users by optional case-insensitive partial first-name, last-name, and email filters. Organization admins can view users in their organization; developers can only receive their own account. Responses use createdAt and deletedAt lifecycle fields; any non-null deletedAt is terminal.
Update own profile. All fields optional.
Change own password.
Get the caller's non-deleted organization. Responses use createdAt and deletedAt lifecycle fields; any non-null deletedAt is terminal. The organizationId must match the caller's organization.
Admin-only. Replaces the organization name and address; managed identity, hierarchy, admin, createdAt, and deletedAt fields are preserved.

query.description: invocation token supplied in the lambda input

request.description: Lambda-authenticated. Marks the matching current run as started. Continue execution only when resultCode is 0. Enable the AWS parameters for ASYNC Lambda invocations.

Lambda-authenticated. Returns the current-generation assignment-private binary value, or HTTP 204 when absent. Reset invalidates the private generation. Enable shared to use the unaffected location scope.
Lambda-authenticated. Stores arbitrary bytes in the current assignment-private generation; stale lambda keys are rejected after reset. Enable shared to use the unaffected location scope.
Lambda-authenticated. Deletes an assignment-private variable. Enable shared to delete from the lambda's location scope.
Lambda-authenticated. Creates an OPEN alert after authorizing all referenced resources. Repeating the same idempotency key and payload returns the existing alert with created=false.
List lambda versions. The `trigger` bitmask uses 1 = schedule, 2 = location event, and 4 = device event. Scheduled executions run through the separate `asyncFunction` lane.
Create the next lambda version. `bump` must be `MAJOR`, `MINOR`, or `PATCH`; the server derives the semantic version number. `trigger` configures trigger event types.
Promote the version under test to production and retain the previous production version as the rollback fallback.
Discard the development version currently under test.
Archive the current production version and restore the fallback version to production.
Returns available AWS Lambda Python image tags, including architecture, in `result`.

query.description: required; Python version and processor architecture, such as 3.14-arm64; select a value returned by Get Available Python Image Tags

request.description: Body is a raw zip or tar archive (Content-Type application/zip or application/x-tar). `buildTarget` combines the Python version and processor architecture in `<python-version>-<architecture>` form and must be one of the values returned by Get Available Python Image Tags. Response `requestId` is saved to the `uploadId` variable.

Returns `result.status` (`CREATED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, or `FAILED`) and an optional `result.message`. Poll while the status is `CREATED` or `IN_PROGRESS`; `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` are terminal.
